item.description: Climate-driven environmental change can reorganize marine food webs, yet different components of plankton communities may respond asynchronously to changing hydroclimatic conditions. item.description: Multisequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides a more reliable diagnosis in clinical applications through complementary information across sequences. item.title: Effect of intranasal insulin on postoperative delirium: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Intranasal insulin probably reduces POD in adult surgical patients. The dose-response findings suggest that 30 IU may provide the greatest benefit, with no apparent additional reduction at higher doses. Larger multicentre trials are needed to confirm the optimal regimen and comprehensively evaluate safety.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: LIR practices in Korea have evolved toward simpler, analyzer-centered workflows; however, variability persists in terms of review criteria, workload, reporting, and reimbursements. Therefore, updated consensus recommendations and reimbursement policies are required.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Faster sodium correction was not significantly associated with overall mortality in adults with hypernatremia. item.title: Simple psychiatric screening for burning mouth syndrome and persistent globus pharyngeus using the hospital anxiety and depression scale: a case-control study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patients with BMS or persistent GP had higher levels of anxiety and depression than controls. A brief HADS-based screening proved clinically feasible in an otorhinolaryngology setting by identifying patients with substantial psychiatric burden and facilitating acceptance of psychiatric referral among moderate-to-severe cases. These findings may support the integration of HADS-guided psychiatric screening and referral into routine otorhinolaryngologic care.

item.description: Euripides' The Bacchae dramatizes the devastating consequences of Dionysian ecstasy and the quiet human response that follows. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a significant SRB decline in South Korea. The nine-month lag observed in the Daegu epicenter aligns with a pre-fertilization mechanism, consistent with the exploratory hypothesis that acute societal stress may disproportionately impair Y-bearing sperm viability. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest SRB serves as a sensitive population-level indicator of societal distress.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this large nationwide general population cohort, BMI showed a J-shaped association with mortality from aortic aneurysm and dissection. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this first high-volume, single-center real-world experience of PFA in South Korea, PFA was associated with favorable procedural efficiency and a low complication profile. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective pilot study, intraoperative 5-ALA-based PDD was feasible and safe in breast cancer specimens. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Primary GP5 was associated with unfavorable oncological outcomes in low-volume de novo mHSPC treated with upfront ARPI-based doublet therapy. Its prognostic significance and potential role in guiding treatment intensification require further validation.

item.title: Self-reported eating speed and the risk of breast cancer among Japanese women: a retrospective cohort study from the LIFE Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this large cohort, slower self-reported eating speed was associated with a modestly lower risk of incident breast cancer. By providing one of the first large-scale longitudinal evaluations of the association between self-reported eating speed and breast cancer risk, this study addresses a gap in epidemiological evidence but does not establish that slower eating prevents breast cancer.

item.title: Pharmacotherapy for older adults with cancer: a digest of the Japanese clinical practice guidelines (2nd edition) - lung cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These guidelines provide practical, evidence-based recommendations for pharmacotherapy in older adults with lung cancer. They emphasize individualized treatment strategies based on patient characteristics, treatment goals, and tolerability. Further research in older populations is required to strengthen the evidence base for geriatric oncology.
